extracted.intended_audience: authors/developers of GAP packages (GAP package authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for structuring, documenting, testing, and packaging a GAP package so it integrates into GAP and can be redistributed or deposited. Covers directory layout, required metadata (PackageInfo.g), documentation and test formats, kernel modules, naming conventions, and tooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package directory structure and required files
rubrics_metrics.description: A GAP package's files must be collected in a single directory (packagedir). packagedir should be an alphanumeric name (no whitespace) and be a subdirectory of a pkg directory in one of the GAP root directories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended layout: packagedir/ with subdirectories doc/, lib/, tst/, and files CHANGES, LICENSE, README, PackageInfo.g, init.g, read.g. PackageInfo.g and init.g must be present; read.g is optional. If package contains compiled code, use src and possibly include configure/Makefile.in. Use lib for GAP code (.g, .gd, .gi). The package home directory is typically packagename (optionally converted to lowercase and optionally followed by version). Follow existing package layouts or use the PackageMaker tool to create the structure automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: PackageInfo.g — mandatory components and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Every package must have PackageInfo.g which contains meta-information via SetPackageInfo(record). Certain components of this record are mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Mandatory components (with their required types/formats):
- PackageName: a nonempty string denoting the name of the package
- Subtitle: a string describing package's contents (fit one line)
- Version: a nonempty string that does not start with '=' (see Section 76.18)
- Date: string of form yyyy-mm-dd denoting release date (a date since 1999)
- License: a nonempty string containing an SPDX ID (see Section 76.22)
- ArchiveURL: string starting with http://, https://, or ftp:// (URL to download current package archive, without suffix describing format)
- ArchiveFormats: a string listing supported formats (among .tar.gz, .tar.bz2, -win.zip) separated by whitespace or commas
- README_URL: string starting with http(s)/ftp
- PackageInfoURL: string starting with http(s)/ftp
- AbstractHTML: string describing package contents in a few lines in HTML format
- PackageWWWHome: string starting with http(s)/ftp
- PackageDoc: a record or list of records describing package documentation books (each record with BookName, LongTitle, SixFile, HTMLStart, PDFFile, ArchiveURLSubset)
Ensure these fields conform to the listed formats (e.g., Date format, ArchiveURL prefix).

rubrics_metrics.name: PackageInfo.g — optional components & dependency/contact metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: PackageInfo.g supports many optional components that become relevant for redistribution and integration with GAP's package infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Notable optional components and constraints:
- TextFiles / BinaryFiles / TextBinaryFilesPatterns: lists of strings; at most one of these three may be present; patterns must start with 'T' for text and 'B' for binary.
- Persons: list of records with mandatory LastName and at least one of IsAuthor or IsMaintainer; if IsMaintainer is true then one of Email, WWWHome, or PostalAddress is mandatory; FirstNames, Place, Institution optional.
- SourceRepository: record with Type and URL strings (e.g., "git")
- IssueTrackerURL, SupportEmail: strings (URLs / email)
- Dependencies: record describing dependencies with optional components GAP (string denoting needed GAP version), NeededOtherPackages and SuggestedOtherPackages (lists of [pkgname, pkgversion] pairs)
- ExternalConditions: list of strings or [text, URL] pairs denoting requirements on external programs
- AvailabilityTest: a function returning true if the package is available (default ReturnTrue if only GAP code)
- BannerString / BannerFunction, TestFile, Keywords (list of strings), Extensions (list of records) — may be used for redistribution and package website
Follow the documented shapes for these fields when populating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: ValidatePackageInfo checks and diagnostics
rubrics_metrics.description: ValidatePackageInfo(info) validates a PackageInfo.g record or file and reports incorrect components or missing required fields; if info is a filename it also checks that files mentioned exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ValidatePackageInfo returns true if format is correct, false otherwise, and prints diagnostics about incorrect components. Diagnostic messages can be suppressed by setting the global option quiet to true. Use this to detect missing fields before distribution. Example diagnostics show exact components missing or malformed (e.g., 'component Date must be bound to a string of the form yyyy-mm-dd').

rubrics_metrics.name: README content and location
rubrics_metrics.description: A package should include a README (optionally README.txt or README.md) in the package home directory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: README should contain installation instructions (including ways of getting the package), how to install, names of package authors and their email addresses. These installation instructions should be repeated or referenced in the package documentation in doc/.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHANGES file recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a CHANGES file (optionally with .txt or .md) recording main changes between package versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for maintainers and users to track what changed between releases. Not strictly required but recommended for future versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: LICENSE file / licensing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a license file explaining the distribution terms of the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should make clear licensing terms (what users are allowed to copy, modify, redistribute). The License component in PackageInfo.g should contain an SPDX ID. GAP itself uses GPLv2; authors are encouraged to consider GPL but may choose other licenses. Filename may be LICENSE, COPYING, GPL, etc., with optional extension .txt or .md.

rubrics_metrics.name: init.g and read.g and declaration/implementation split
rubrics_metrics.description: Every GAP package must have init.g. Typical init.g and read.g should consist of ReadPackage commands to read further files; if declaration and implementation are separated, use read.g for implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended separation: declaration files (.gd) for names/headers to be read in init.g, implementation files (.gi) with definitions read in read.g. This allows implementations to refer to names declared earlier. Package code should go in lib/ and ReadPackage/Read commands used as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: lib / src / doc / tst directories roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard roles for package subdirectories: lib for GAP source code, src for non-GAP source (e.g., C), doc for documentation (GAPDoc format), tst for tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: lib is the preferred place for .g/.gd/.gi files; src holds C code and may have an include directory for .h files. doc should contain GAPDoc XML-based manual (master main.xml, chapter .xml files, makedocrel.g to build). tst should contain test files; for deposited packages, a basic test may be specified in PackageInfo.g to be included in GAP's standard test suite; heavier/time-consuming tests should remain in tst with instructions on how to run them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation format: GAPDoc and distribution formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Package documentation should be prepared in the GAPDoc XML-based format and provided in terminal-friendly text and printable PDF, with optional HTML for browsing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum provide a text version usable in GAP's terminal and a PDF. HTML via GAPDoc is recommended; HTML manual can support MathJax for high-quality math rendering. To produce PDF you need pdflatex. Provide a manual.bib (BibTeX database) or xml in BibXMLext format. AutoDoc may be used to simplify documentation generation. Alternative older TeX-based systems exist but are not recommended for new packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests: presence, format and standard-suite inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages are highly recommended to include test files in tst/. Deposited packages may specify a test file to be included in GAP's standard test suite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide at least a basic test verifying package functionality and manual examples. Tests that are more specific or time-consuming should remain in tst with instructions and not be part of the standard release test suite. See Section 76.19 for requirements and formats for test files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel modules and compiled components
rubrics_metrics.description: If a package has a kernel module (C code), it can be compiled using the gac script and loaded appropriately; packages must handle availability of kernel modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gac -d to produce dynamically loadable modules (e.g., gap4/gac -d test.c produces test.so). Use LoadKernelExtension(pkgname[, modname]) to locate and load the kernel module (preferred over older LoadDynamicModule), and IsKernelExtensionAvailable(pkgname[, modname]) in AvailabilityTest to check availability. If kernel extension is required, PackageInfo.g should define an AvailabilityTest that calls IsKernelExtensionAvailable. Recommend naming kernel extension to match package name when possible; otherwise provide second argument to LoadKernelExtension to specify module name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid defining global functions/variables via direct assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not define package functions and variables by direct assignment in the interactive style (e.g., Squared := x -> x^2;;), because such definitions are easily overwritten without warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect globals by using BindGlobal, DeclareGlobalFunction / InstallGlobalFunction pairs, or DeclareGlobalVariable / InstallValue. These mechanisms help avoid accidental overwriting and provide safer global declarations. Use Declare.../Install... pairs for operations, methods, attributes and properties where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming conventions to avoid clashes
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose names for functions and variables that begin with a string identifying the package to reduce accidental overwriting and name clashes with other packages or the GAP library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefixing identifiers (e.g., Eg... in the Example package) helps avoid clashes and accidental user overwrites. Since GAP 4.5, packages may place global variables into a local namespace by using identifiers ending with '@' (e.g., xYz@); such variables are accessible externally only by full name (xYz@YourPackageName), aiding compatibility. Operations and methods generally do not need such prefixing because multiple methods for the same operation are supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: File header and code style conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Package files may follow GAP library style: start with a header listing filename, copyright, short description and authors, and end with a comment line #E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indentation and decorative spacing are up to authors, but global comments are usually indented by two hash marks and two blanks. Separate declarations, method or function installations with a header. Use GAPDoc inclusion facilities to distribute documentation fragments across source files. AutoDoc may be used to generate documentation annotations inside source files (#! @Arguments ... etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Including empty directories in package distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need an empty directory to be present in the distribution (e.g., as a runtime data place), ensure it is included explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to put a short README file in such empty directories describing its purpose to ensure the directory is included in the redistribution archives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using PackageMaker to create package skeletons
rubrics_metrics.description: The PackageMaker tool (https://github.com/gap-system/PackageMaker) can generate a basic GAP package skeleton and a template PackageInfo.g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PackageMaker asks questions about the intended package and populates a new directory with files needed for a basic package. Use the Example package's PackageInfo.g as a well-commented prototype, and inspect it via Pager(StringFile(Filename(DirectoriesLibrary(), "../pkg/example/PackageInfo.g"))).

rubrics_metrics.name: ShowPackageVariables / PackageVariablesInfo behavior and customization
rubrics_metrics.description: ShowPackageVariables(pkgname[, version][, arec]) prints global variables and methods that become bound when a package is loaded (it actually loads the package). PackageVariablesInfo(pkgname, version) collects this information without the interactive display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If version is given, that version is considered. An error is printed if the package/version is not available or already loaded. Info lines for undocumented variables are marked with an asterisk *. The following are omitted: default setter methods for attributes/properties declared in the package, and Setattr/Hasattr type variables. The output can be customized via arec with components: show (list of kinds to show, e.g., 'new global functions'), showDocumented (true/false), showUndocumented (true/false), showPrivate (true/false), Display (function to show strings, default Print; Pager available). BrowsePackageVariables (from Browse package) can present interactive output using PackageVariablesInfo as input.
